summary: Milestone 2026.09.665 completed 8 experiments, all compute-bound, in 7.2 wall-time minutes. The longest task was 'Refine cross-game supervisor selection from actual redirect outcomes' at 2.39 minutes, followed by 'Measure direct native service cost and preserve board dispositions' at 1.46 minutes and 'Reconcile fourteen dispositions and select the next scientific question' at 1.09 minutes. Sub-phase timing was not recorded within these runs to separate model inference duration from validation scaffolding or serialization overhead.
bottlenecks_identified: 'Refine cross-game supervisor selection from actual redirect outcomes' took the longest at 2.39 minutes out of 7.2 total wall-time minutes (approx. 33% of milestone duration), but lacks granular sub-phase telemetry to separate model inference latency from validation scaffolding and disk serialization.

'Measure direct native service cost and preserve board dispositions' (1.46 minutes) and 'Reconcile fourteen dispositions and select the next scientific question' (1.09 minutes) combined with the longest task to account for 4.94 minutes (approx. 69% of milestone wall time) without recorded intra-task phase durations.

The top 5 experiments accounted for 6.32 out of 7.2 total wall-time minutes (approx. 88% of milestone duration), with task durations reconstructed from disk mtimes rather than continuous execution logging.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated post-completion snapshot (PID 2365987 on GPU 0 with 17892MB allocated at 0% utilization), leaving active-window GPU utilization unmeasured while gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is false.
Experiment task records did not log model concurrency or runner dispatch receipts, though all completed tasks were single-model workloads where DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch is not applicable.
improvements_suggested: Instrument granular sub-phase duration timers and monotonic stage logging inside compute-bound tasks to isolate model inference latency from validation scaffolding and serialization overhead.

Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound executions to sample live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active compute windows rather than relying on point-in-time post-run snapshots.
Record explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to verify DualGPURunner eligibility whenever two or more models run concurrently.
Implement runtime milestone-scoped execution logging to avoid reliance on post-hoc disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration timers and per-stage progress logging inside the supervisor selection and native service measurement pipelines.
Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound task execution to record live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active execution windows.
Emit explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to audit DualGPURunner engagement on multi-model workloads.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed 8 compute-bound tasks in 7.2 wall-time minutes, with execution concentrated in cross-game supervisor selection refinement (2.39 minutes), direct native service cost measurement (1.46 minutes), and fourteen-disposition reconciliation (1.09 minutes). The post-run GPU monitor report confirms an idle llama.cpp process on GPU 0 after completion but cannot evaluate active-window compute efficiency, and because only single-model tasks were executed, no DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch opportunity was missed. Sub-phase timing and continuous execution telemetry are necessary next steps to identify actionable latency optimizations.
